honest_c3: C1 mac CPU fp32 — same substrate as BG-BR; numerical drift inside ULP of logit-lens BG-AR run.
C2 single-prompt-per-language — broader corpus may shift dominance distribution; one prompt per family is anecdotal not population.

C3 char-class breakdown counts Unicode blocks, NOT semantic coherence. A chinese=20 emit can still be unrelated/incoherent characters; this probe answers 'which script' not 'which language is fluent'.

C4 max_new=25 token cap — substrate may not have warmed up at 25 tokens; longer-horizon emit could shift dominance. Also emit may include sentencepiece pieces decoded into joined text where length stats are coupled to BPE subword distribution.

C5 'mixed_ko_en' and 'punctuation' / 'numbers' / 'code_*' prompts have no single 'matching language' so dominance there is pure substrate- bias not a match-test. 'numbers' should ideally favor digits if the substrate respects context; if not, it indicates broader substrate collapse to a fixed token-class bias regardless of input.
